quarterly_data.signal: Head of U.S. Oncology Commercial Chumi Khurana on the first-line HER2+ GEA launch of Ziihera (zanidatamab), launched about three weeks earlier: HER2 testing rates in GEA are 'somewhere around 80%', but trastuzumab 'is only used in about 60% of the patients that are eligible', so the focus is driving HER2-directed treatment toward 100% of HER2-positive patients. She restated the U.S. GEA incidence of 8,000 patients and 3,000 to 4,000 treatable after the unresectable frontline label filter and testing. 'We're two weeks into the launch, so we don't really have any data yet'; there are 'no barriers to ramp up' (established J-code, sales force already in place, supply, JazzCares running, no payer barriers), and reaching peak 'usually takes about a year or two'. NCCN guideline inclusion is expected 'any day now' but is not a barrier to uptake. Competing HER2 ADCs and bispecifics are 'a few years out', with data 'towards the end of the decade'.
quarterly_data.figure: HER2 testing around 80%; trastuzumab used in about 60% of eligible patients; 8,000 U.S. GEA incidence; 3,000 to 4,000 treatable; peak usually about a year or two

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jack Spinks on the raised zanidatamab peak-sales range: 'we did provide a range of $3 billion-$5 billion' and 'recognize that there are risks inherent to drug development'; reaching the high end depends on breadth - late-line breast, early breast, colorectal and non-small cell lung cancer - and replacing trastuzumab. Khurana said the increase reflects the GEA data plus added indications (CRC, lung, early breast and metastatic breast with TKIs). Zanidatamab's first-line GEA launch contributes only about a month in Q3 and a full fourth quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: zanidatamab peak sales range $3 billion-$5 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Modeyso (dordaviprone): Khurana cited a communicated peak sales figure of $500 million, which CFO Jack Spinks specified as '$500 million+ in the U.S.' covering first and second line; the ACTION trial 'would serve as the basis for submission ex-U.S. as well', with the readout hoped for 'in the first half of 2027'. Real-world duration of therapy is still being assessed and is a potential inflection point.
quarterly_data.figure: Modeyso peak sales $500 million+ in the U.S.; ACTION readout first half of 2027

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jack Spinks on XYWAV in idiopathic hypersomnia: 'I think we have close to 6,000 patients today, but we do see that that market's potentially as big as narcolepsy.' He views orexin-2 agonists as complementary wake-promoting agents in NT1 rather than replacements, since XYWAV improves nighttime sleep. On business development he said Jazz 'just closed the Actio acquisition', which builds on its epilepsy strength, and that net leverage was 'maybe less than one time' last quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: close to 6,000 XYWAV IH patients; net leverage less than one time
